chapter: Dana Valery and the Glenn Miller band
title: Drummer-conductor for singer Dana Valery
summary: Dana Valery hires him to travel and conduct her band for a year, including the Persian Room; he quits to join Glenn Miller.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Yeah, we had a bunch of things, I can’t remember. But what happened was a girl singer came in named Dana Valery and that’s spelled D-A-N-A. A lot of people called her Dana Valerie but it was [pronounced Donna Va lerie] and she was Sergio Franchi’s sister. Her real name was Falstagali, they’re from Johannesberg, South Africa. Sergio Franchi was at the time, he’s since passed away, he was kind of like a Mario Lanza kind of singer. And she was looking for a conductor. She wanted somebody to travel with her. She was doing it on her own, she was kind of up-and-coming. But she didn’t want a piano — she wanted a drummer, because every time she went someplace the drummers were not up to what she wanted. But here I am playing bass on her show. But somebody said, “no this guy’s a great drummer.” Well, somebody said, “he’s a fine drummer.” So I said, “well why don’t you come down to my house and have some spaghetti, my mother will cook it for you,” which impressed her. Anyway I went on the road with her for a year, 1969, I traveled with her. We went to California, Mr. Kelly’s in Chicago, we did The Washington in Puerto Rico, whatever. But we did the Persian Room in New York City. And here I am, the drummer, conducting the band. So I had to learn how to — I had taken conducting classes, which is one-two-three-four-one, but I had to learn how to do it in just reverse and play with the right hand — let’s see, I can’t remember even how — one-two-three- four-one. So I had to get all these conducting things down like that. So I was their drummer-conductor for a year. And it was fairly interesting but I had also, prior to that, done a week or a few days with Buddy DeFranco’s Glenn Miller Orchestra, but had to go back with Dana Valery. And the call came — Dana came up and spent Christmas, she and her husband of the time, came up to our house and stayed there, put a nice little gift under the tree for me, and as soon as she got back to New York I called and quit.
